author_reading_scope: Inspected the complete full-text bodies of the 9-page Goodfellow et al. paper and the 6-page Yingzhen Li lecture note. The GAN proof-relevant passages are Goodfellow §§3–4.1, Proposition 1, Theorem 1, equations (1)–(6), PDF pp. 2–5; and Li §§1.1–1.2, equations (1)–(11), PDF pp. 1–2. Also read Goodfellow §4.2, including Proposition 2 and the final finite-MLP limitation, and the remaining lecture-note pages for scope. The published local mathematical suppliers and the complete relevant proof arguments used for measurability, scalar optimization, integral linearity and equality cases were inspected at their actual item bodies. Each harvested source result and its disposition is recorded in batch-60.coverage.json.

sources.title: Ian J. Goodfellow et al., Generative Adversarial Nets, arXiv:1406.2661v1

author_read_locators.locator: Complete paper; §3, equation (1); §4.1, Proposition 1, Theorem 1, equations (2)–(6), PDF pp. 2–5.
author_read_locators.disposition: Used the source objective, density-level discriminator claim and JS/global-optimum identities as the target. The local pointwise proof handles all zero-density branches; the local lemma supplies the nonnegativity/equality proof that the paper cites but omits. The disjoint-support arithmetic is verified locally.

author_read_locators.locator: Complete §4.2, Proposition 2 and final paragraph, PDF p. 5.
author_read_locators.disposition: Used only to preserve the boundary between the nonparametric distribution-space claim and finite MLP training. Proposition 2 assumes enough capacity, an optimal discriminator at every step and sufficiently small criterion-improving distribution updates. The exact scalar six-step cycle is original local verification and is not attributed to this paper.

sources.title: Yingzhen Li, Lecture notes on generative adversarial networks (GANs), Deep Learning (Winter 2022, Imperial College London)

author_read_locators.disposition: Independent lecture-note treatment of binary cross-entropy, GAN objective, ideal-discriminator formula and JS substitution. Its parameter-gradient derivation is not used as a proof of unrestricted pointwise maximization; the authored proof performs the pointwise optimization directly. The notes assert the JS divergence property without proving it; the local lemma supplies that argument.

author_read_locators.locator: Complete note §§1.3–1.4 and remaining pages, PDF pp. 2–6.
author_read_locators.disposition: Read for scope only. Conditional GAN and Wasserstein GAN variants are outside ML-55. The note gives no exact finite-game cycle; no such result is attributed to it.
